articles.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Day 1
articles.author: TechCrunch Events
articles.content:
Day 1 ofTechCrunch Disrupt 2026is officially underway, bringing together 10,000+ startup founders, investors, and tech leaders under one roof at San Francisco’s Moscone West. Big ideas are colliding, connections are forming at every turn, and the startup ecosystem’s most influential voices are driving the conversation.

FromStartup Battlefieldto six new industry stages focused on scaling, AI, fintech, climate tech, and more, Disrupt is packed with game-changing perspectives and opportunities. The next partnership, investment, or breakout company could emerge from any meeting, session, or coffee line conversation.Meet the 250+ speakersshaping the discussion.

Grab your ticket nowso you don’t miss a moment at Disrupt. There’s still a little time to grab your pass and be at this annual startup event.

Registration hours:7:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

Stop by the registration desk in the Level 1 lobby of Moscone West to register in person or pick up your scannable event badge. The badge features Klik technology, which makes it easy to exchange contact information with people you scan your badge with. Using the event app, you can access and keep those contacts even after the event ends.

Explore 300+ exhibiting startups showcasing cutting-edge technologies across industries. This is the center of Disrupt, where 10,000+ attendees converge to discover new breakthroughs and spark new connections.

Haven’t registered yet? You still can — but don’t wait, or you will miss out.Grab your ticket nowand walk straight into the action: six industry stages, interactive roundtables, Q&A breakouts, hundreds of exhibiting startups, investor-founder meetings, AI-powered matchmaking networking, and Side Events lighting up the Bay Area tech scene all week long.

Make your way to the Pitch Showcase Stage at the back of the Expo Hall to experience one of the most electrifying formats on the conference floor: rapid-fire, one-minute lightning pitches from some of the most promising startups representing their home countries and regions.

The Startup Battlefield 200 Built World category showcases the most innovative early-stage startups tackling major challenges in real estate, construction, architecture, smart cities, and infrastructure. Discover the technologies transforming the physical spaces where we live, work, and play. Stop by to catch their lightning pitches and meet the bold entrepreneurs building what’s next.

The spotlight also shines on Startup Battlefield, TechCrunch’s renowned “World Series of pitch competitions.” After vetting thousands of applicants, TechCrunch selected the top 20 early-stage startups to pitch in front of some of the world’s most seasoned VCs. They’ll compete for a $100,000 equity-free prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup.

The Startup Battlefield 200 Sustainability category highlights the most groundbreaking early-stage companies tackling the world’s most urgent environmental and climate challenges, from renewable energy and carbon capture to circular economy platforms, sustainable agriculture, clean water solutions, and beyond.

These are the founders turning bold climate commitments into real-world technology, building businesses that prove profitability and planetary impact are not mutually exclusive — and they’re making their case in just two minutes. Stop by, catch their lightning pitches, and meet the startups that are determined to leave the world better than they found it.

From physical AI and the future of intelligent systems to fundraising, hiring, and scaling breakout companies, today’s speakers are tackling the opportunities and challenges shaping the next generation of startups. Here’s a look at what’s happening across the stages today.Check out the full agenda, which includes 200+ sessions.

The Startup Battlefield — Space and Physical AI:Judges include Anu Bharadwaj (Iconiq), Sara Deshpande (Maven Ventures), Benjamin Narasin (Tenacity Venture Capital), Aatish Nayak (Kleiner Perkins), Michael Palank (MaC Venture Capital).

Building the Impossible:RJ Scaringe (Rivian).

The Startup Battlefield — Energy and Manufacturing:Caleb Appleton (Bison Ventures), Feyza Haskaraman (Felicis), Sho Sho Leigha Ho (General Catalyst), Leah Solivan (Precedent.vc).

Can AI Keep Scaling?:Andrew Feldman (Cerebras Systems).

Beyond Screens:Max Hodak (Science Corporation).

Equity Live: The Startup Stories Shaping 2026:TechCrunch’s Equity podcast takes the Builders Stage for a live recording from Disrupt. Join the Equity team as they break down the biggest startup, venture, and technology stories of the moment and what they mean for founders and investors heading into 2027.

What Happens When OpenAI Ships Your Roadmap:Rob Toews (Radical Ventures), Linda Tong (Webflow), Michel Tricot (Airbyte).

The Rise of Agentic AI: Lessons for Hardware Founders:Ziad Asghar (Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.), Florence Ion (PCMag).

Competing for AI Talent: Pay, Equity, and Retention:Matt Birnbaum (Wylder.co), Ioana Hreninciuc (Runware), Atli Thorkelsson (Redpoint Ventures).

The Builder’s Playbook: What Founders Need to Win the Agentic Era:Stephan Bitton (Google Cloud).

PMF Red Flags: How to Tell If You Really Have It:Anu Bharadwaj (Iconiq), Rajeev Dham (Sapphire Ventures), Rahul Vohra (Superhuman).

From MVP to Billions of Users: How Product Decisions Must Change at Scale:Robby Stein (Google).

When Machines Clock In (Hosted by NYSE Wired):Brian Baumann (New York Stock Exchange), Dr. Adam Campbell (Gatik), Samir Menon (Dexterity AI), Sankaet Pathak (Foundation Future Industries, Inc.).

Hiring When AI Is a Co-founder:Michelle Johnson (Insight Partners), John Koelliker (Leland), Josh Reeves (Gusto).

The Future of Money Movement in the Agentic Economy:Nikhil Chandhok (Circle), Rodney Robinson (TabaPay, Inc.), Carlotta (Lotti) Siniscalco (Emergence Capital).

AI, Trust & Verification in Financial Services:Hannah Bozian (American Express), Pedro Sanzovo (Plaid), Victoria Zuo (QED Investors).

Winning the Modern Financial Consumer:Abhishek Fatehpuria (Robinhood).

Where the AI Infrastructure Boom Is Creating Winners:Ben Longmier (Ambrosia Energy), Bill Thayer (Bloom Energy).

When the Energy Gets Smart: What Vertical AI Actually Delivers at Scale:Deepak Garg (SEW.AI), Paul Lau (SMUD).

How Twilio’s Founder Is Tackling the Power Problem:Jeff Lawson (Twilio).

Bringing Fusion to the Grid:David Kirtley (Helion), Brandon Sorbom (Commonwealth Fusion Systems).

Rewiring the Grid for the Electric Age:Apoorv Bhargava (Weave Grid, Inc.), Kristin Eberhard (Rewiring America), Tim Heidel (VEIR).

Located at the end of the Expo Hall, breakout sessions include a panel of experts on the presented topic, with room at the end for attendees to ask direct questions. See the full three-day lineup in theDisrupt agenda.

What Is Physical AI, Anyway?:Susan Schofer (SOSV HAX), Parikshit Sharma (SOSV SF), Duncan Turner (SOSV HAX), Pae Wu (SOSV SF).

The New Job of the Data Team Is Providing Context to AI:George Fraser (Fivetran + dbt Labs).

The Quantum Revolution: What Investors and Builders Need to Know:Andrew Dzurak (Diraq).

Taiwan Powering the Next AI Revolution: Connect, Invest & Scale:Michelle Chan (Phison Electronics USA), BoGaun Chen (ITRI International), Erica Lin (ITRI International), Mingche Wang (ITRI International).

How to Build AI We Can Trust:Robbie Goldfarb (Forum AI).

The Inference Economy: Why AI’s Next Trillion Dollars Won’t Look Like Its First:Hagay Lupesko (Cerebras Systems), Ali Mahmoud (Glasswing Ventures).

These small-group sessions give founders and investors the chance to tackle real-world challenges up close. Remember: Pre-registration on the event app is required for entry.Visit the Disrupt agendato see all the roundtable sessions for the next three days.

Arm Wrestling Your Data: The Physical AI Challenge:Radha Basu (iMerit).

Can AI Take You Public? The New Playbook for IPO-Ready Finance:Eléonore Crespo (Pigment), Sofia Fatakhova (Chime).

AI’s Next Frontier: Modernizing Legacy Industries:Rob Biederman (Asymmetric Capital Partners).

Atoms vs. Bits: Physical AI for the Physical World:Jackson Feder (MetaProp).

Beyond Inventory: The Commerce AI Playbook for the Intent Era:Srishti Chaudhary (Walmart eCommerce).

Healthcare Took 40 Years to Adopt EHRs, Then Adopted Generative AI in Three. What Comes Next?:Brian Butler (Questa Capital).

From Pilot to Production at Scale: Provable, Trusted Agentic AI for the Enterprise:Dr. Maha Achour (Kodamai), Pankaj Kedia (2468 Ventures), Yasser Shaaban (Humain).

Specialty Post-Training Data: Powering the Next Wave of AI:Dani London (Base10 Partners).

The Science of Powerful Introductions: How to Be Remembered in an AI World:Cal Amir (Introduction Lab).

Beyond the Demo: Building Physical AI That Actually Works:Logan Farrell (Rugged Robotics), Austin Yount (Brick & Mortar Ventures).

Labs or Factory Floors: Who Will Win Physical AI?:Matt Burns (Insight Media Group), Roman Hölzl (RobCo).

Beyond the Term Sheet: How to Architect a Great Fundraise:Weston Moyer (MVP Ventures).

Brutal Truth: 12 Critical Mistakes That Nearly Derailed My CISO Career:Stephen Ward (Brightmind Partners).

Networking Lounge powered by Signify Business Cash World Elite Mastercard® by Wells Fargo:Open 9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Find your next co-founder, investor, or mentor through meetings you schedule via the event app or spontaneous meetups.

Deal Flow Café:Opens at 9:00 a.m. Exclusive to founders and investors, providing a quiet space to make deals over coffee.

Company-hostedSide Eventsare happening throughout San Francisco this week, extending the Disrupt energy well beyond Moscone West. Here are a few events happening tonight — panels, parties, and meetups designed to connect founders, investors, and innovators across every corner of tech. Make sure to RSVP for your spot at any of these. Explore thefull lineup of Side Eventsand fill your schedule with more time for connections and insights.

The Irish Shark Tank: Hosted by Enterprise Ireland

SafetyWing Happy Hour at Harrington’s: Hosted by SafetyWing

Born2Global Founder Networking Night: Hosted by WayFounder

There’s still some time left to register for your pass and explore all these activations.Get your ticket now. There’s still so much more to experience at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 — including more Startup Battlefield pitches, game-changing sessions, and unforgettable connections. Tickets are available through the final day. Secure yours now and be part of the future of tech. Do not wait.

articles.title: The 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20: From organs to orbit and everything in between
articles.author: Isabelle Johannessen
articles.content:
Twenty founders just earned their shot at Disrupt glory. They’re headed to the Disrupt Stage atTechCrunch Disruptto compete for the $100,000 prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup.

Every year, thousands of founders from around the world pitch us on what they believe the future should look like. This year’s Top 20 are building it from organs to orbit and everywhere in between.

Across this cohort, one theme kept emerging: Making the previously invisible measurable.

These founders are finding ways to understand signals we couldn’t previously capture, model systems too complex to predict, and turn the physical world into data that machines can actually act on. They’re measuring the biological clocks inside our bodies and growing miniature human organs in labs. They’re teaching robots to take on increasingly complex physical work and modeling the real world closely enough to predict what might happen next — even the behavior of wild animals. They’re extracting intelligence from scam calls and finding new ways to use the computing power already orbiting above our heads.

And then, of course, there’s the company trying to launch cargo into space with a giant hydrogen-powered cannon.

Subtle, this group is not.

What connects these 20 companies isn’t a single technology or industry. It’s an ambition to understand more of the world around us — biological, physical, industrial, and digital — and use that understanding to make better decisions, automate what once required human intervention, and tackle problems that previously seemed too complex to solve.

Now they have six minutes on the Disrupt Stage to prove it.

Here are the 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20.

Longshot Space: Reinventing the economics of space by launching cargo to orbit at $50/kg using hydrogen-powered kinetic launchers.

Veritas: Protecting luxury brands with custom microchips that verify authenticity and enable connected post-purchase experiences.

Laplace Intelligence:Building agentic world models that help cities, ports, and airports roll out counterfactual futures of the real world before they act.

Flox Intelligence:Preventing deadly wildlife collisions at airports and railways with real-time AI that detects animal behavior and safely redirects them.

Satlyt:Helping satellite operators unlock and monetize idle compute by transforming their spacecraft into virtual AI data centers with a single line of code.

LNK Energies: Delivering clean hydrogen power cheaper than diesel through breakthrough compact reactor technology compatible with existing diesel infrastructure.

Helix Carbon:Helping steelmakers cut emissions and fuel costs by electrochemically upcycling blast furnace waste gas into replacement fossil fuels on-site.

IndustrialNext: Automating high-precision, contact-rich assembly tasks by deploying AI-driven robotic systems that learn from production data and adapt to new products.

Niobia AI:Helping process and materials engineers compress weeks of root-cause analysis into minutes with domain-expert AI reasoning.

Licube:Producing ultra-high purity lithium and lithium isotopes (Li-6/Li-7), the critical inputs for nuclear fusion and advanced materials.

Mosqitter:Detecting and preventing mosquito-borne disease spread with real-time disease intelligence platforms that turn sensor networks into early warning systems for national health agencies.

Hiyd AI:Delivering proactive health insights by combining sleep, movement, and nutrition data through an ultra-slim, discreet wearable tracker and AI app.

TimeTeller GmbH:Measuring people’s biological clocks to determine optimal treatment timing through molecular diagnostics and AI, improving efficacy and reducing side effects.

NTangible:Helping coaches and front offices make smarter recruiting decisions by quantifying how athletes perform under pressure with a validated cognitive score.

Intero Biosystems:Accelerating drug development by producing miniature human organs that enable pharma companies to identify safer, more effective medications while reducing clinical trial costs.

Apate.ai:Dismantling scam operations by deploying conversational AI bots that engage scammers and turn their interactions into real-time intelligence for banks, telcos, and governments.

CedarDB: Delivering the data layer for the AI age — real-time transactions and analytics in one engine with guardrails inside the database system that AI agents can’t bypass.

Prismm: Helping banks retain deposits and relationships across generations by automating secure inheritance workflows and financial continuity infrastructure.

Floqer:Streamlining B2B sales by enriching customer data across 80+ sources and stitching every interaction into one millisecond-retrievable timeline for AI agents to act on.

GUDEA: Delivering immediate, actionable insights into audience behavior, engagement patterns, and how information spreads to give organizations a competitive edge in communication management.

After four semifinal sessions across two days, five companies will advance to the Startup Battlefield Finals on Thursday, October 15.

Before the finalists take the stage at 11:30 a.m., we’ll welcomeGlīd,Nephrogen, andMolecule.oneback to the Disrupt Stage for an alumni update on what’s happened since their time in Startup Battlefield.

Then, at 4:15 p.m., one company will be crowned the 2026 Startup Battlefield champion, taking home $100,000 and the Disrupt Cup.

Feeling the FOMO? It’s not too late.Grab a last-minute Disrupt ticket for 50% offand watch it all unfold live.

Startup Battlefield is proudly supported by Google for Startups and SAP.

articles.title: Bumble agrees to a $1.3B acquisition deal as online dating faces a reset
articles.author: Lauren Forristal
articles.content:
Bumble is getting a new owner. The dating appannouncedTuesday that it has agreed to a $1.3 billion acquisition deal with Ithaca Holdings, marking a major shift for a company that once looked like one of the biggest success stories in online dating.

The deal would take the company private after years of declining subscriber numbers, falling revenue, and mounting pressure to rethink the online dating experience. The move may give Bumble a chance to work on its next chapter away from the pressure of public markets.

Founded in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, Bumble made a name for itself for its unique approach where only women made the first move. That helped it stand out in a crowded dating market, and the company eventually went public in 2021 at a valuation of roughly $14 billion.

Since then, however, the dating app landscape has changed considerably. Bumble has faced declining paying users, weaker revenue, and growing dissatisfaction with the familiar swipe-based model. The company recentlyreportedsecond-quarter 2026 revenue of $211 million, down 15.2% year over year, while its paying user base fell 16.4% to approximately 3.2 million.

The acquisition follows a review of strategic options by an independent committee of Bumble’s board, which recommended the transaction after consulting outside legal and financial advisers. Wolfe Herd did not participate in the board’s discussions or vote on the deal, according to the press release.

“In Ithaca, we have found a partner who shares our vision, believes in our women-first mission, and is committed to investing in Bumble’s future,” Wolfe Herd said in a statement.

She also confirmed that she plans to stay actively involved in the business, working alongside Ithaca’s Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman, and the Bumble team.

Going private might give Bumble more flexibility to experiment with new features and make changes without having to answer to public-market investors every quarter. The company has been exploring AI-driven features and putting more energy into helping people connect offline, reflecting a broader shift in how younger users approach dating.

One example isPlans, announced in July, which focuses on bringing people together through real-world activities. Wolfe Herd also recentlyrevealedthat the company is developing a new way for users to interact that could eventually replace the swipe-based model.

articles.title: Apple makes another push into the smart home market with HomeView
articles.author: Lauren Forristal
articles.content:
Apple is taking a big swing at the smart home market. The company on Tuesdayunveiledits long-rumored smart home hub, dubbed HomeView, that can act as a central control point for smart home devices, be used for FaceTime calls, playing music, watching videos, displaying photo slideshows, and more.

The new $299 device looks like a cuboid version of the HomePod, but with a display added to the front. The HomeView comes in two versions: one can sit on a countertop, and the other can be mounted on a wall. Measuring 7 inches wide, the hub features a single FaceTime camera on the front, and has microphones and speakers built into its base.

Apple has preloaded the device with several of its apps, including Calendar, Messages, Photos, FaceTime, Notes, Reminders, Music, and Podcasts. That means users won’t need to reach for their iPhone if they want to check a calendar appointment, send a message, play some music, or look at photos.

Apple sees the device being particularly useful in places such as the kitchen. Someone cooking dinner, for example, could pull up a recipe, watch a video, check a calendar, or start a FaceTime call without resorting to their phone.

It’ll also act as a smart home dashboard, allowing users to ask Siri to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, turn on lights, and lock doors. This comes as Apple announced its lineup of smart home accessories today, including a smart deadbolt lock, security cameras, and doorbell. Users will hear a chime from their HomeView when someone is at the door, for example.

One of the more interesting aspects of the device is how it works with different members of a household.

The hub runs Apple’s updated Siri AI assistant and can recognize individual people in the house. Once it identifies someone, the screen can show information meant for that person, such as their messages, contacts, calendar appointments, notes, and preferred apps. The experience changes automatically when another family member walks up to the device.

The company says HomeView can recognize up to six people.

HomeView puts Apple in a much more direct fight with Amazon and Google, both of which already have established smart display products: Amazon has its Echo Show line, while Google offers the Nest Hub.

Apple has had a mixed history in the smart home space, however, with products such as the HomePod struggling to reach the same level of popularity as competing devices. The new hub is an opportunity for Apple to change that by combining home controls with the company’s wider ecosystem.

The device has been rumored for quite some time, with reports pointing to delays caused in part by problems with Siri AI. Those issues have reportedly affected Apple’s broader smart home plans as well.

This may only be the first phase of Apple’s smart home plan. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has previouslyreportedthat Apple could eventually take the concept further with a more advanced version that features a robotic arm. Such a device could move its display and interact in a more physical way.

Preorders start today, and the device will be available to buy from November 13. It comes in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.

articles.title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.content:
Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. Ina court document, the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.

“Over the past year, Character.ai has taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve its business in the face of significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the board determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the Company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders,” Character.AI CEO Colin Adams said in a statement.

The startup has also agreed to sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million, as well as a non-exclusive perpetual license for its technology.

The company said Disney will provide transition services via former Character.AI employees who joined the entertainment giant last month alongside itsformer CEO Karandeep Singh Anand.

Adams said the company would continue operating during the sale process, which is expected to close in late November or early December. However, he did note that there isn’t yet a bid for the company’s assets or a buyer.

“We hope that the sale process will yield an actionable proposal that will allow continued operations of the Character.ai platform. If such a bid is unavailable, however, the platform will be wound down,” Adams wrote.

Character.AI has had a tumultuous five years. Founded by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer, a co-author of the landmark Transformer paper, and Daniel De Freitas in late 2021, the startup initially focused on training foundation models and developing an AI chatbot platform that lets people create custom characters they could chat with.

By September 2022, the startupreached unicorn valuation with a $150 million fundraiseon the back of high demand for its platform, with the company saying at the time that its users had exchanged more than 2 billion messages with its bots in five months, and active users were averaging more than two hours on the platform daily.

In May 2023, the Character.AI’s appsattractedmore than 1.7 million installs in their first week after launch. But about a year later, in August 2024, Google struck a $2.7 billion deal to license the startup’s models, and both Shazeer and De Freitasreturned to the search giant. At that time, the startup’s general counsel, Dominic Perella, stepped in as interim CEO, and the company moved away from training foundation models to focus on growth.

Character.AI’s traction didn’t slow, however, with its platform recording 20 million monthly active users by October of that year.

But things got difficult after the startup wassuedfollowing the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother says he became obsessed with a chatbot on its platform. Soon after,Texas launched an investigationto assess if the platform conformed to child privacy and safety laws. The company subsequentlysettled some of these lawsuits, added more safety features, and banned minors from its platform.

In June of last year, the company appointed Anand, a former Brex and Meta executive, as CEO, and expanded its products to add AI video generation, and social feeds. The company has since tried to introduce new ways to spur user engagement via interactive storytelling formats as well as microdramas.

But the fact that the company had to file for bankruptcy shows that such changes couldn’t move the needle on sustainability for the startup.

It also shows that consumer-facing AI products are really hard to scale and monetize. Character.AI was one of the top apps in terms of time spent, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. But high engagement can be a double-edged sword; AI costs rise the more people use the app, which consequently also increases the pressure to monetize users.

Character.AI has raised over $193 million in funding across multiple rounds from investors including Lightspeed, SV Angel, Greycroft, and a16z, according to PitchBook.

articles.title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.content:
Personal AI agents are increasingly making transactions on their users’ behalf, but given the nondeterministic nature of large language models, AI bots are prone to doing what they’re not supposed to. Which, in this case, raises the possibility of AI misfiring and making unauthorized transactions.

To get ahead of this problem, American Express is introducing a new framework designed to capture and authenticate a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes the transaction.

The idea is that there should be a way to ensure that the customer’s purchase instructions are carried throughout the transaction lifecycle, Amex says, from the purchase to everything that follows.

Dubbed the “Intent Intelligence Framework,” the company hopes it will become an industry standard for AI-powered transactions.

“These new transactions will have a consumer, a merchant, and an agent,” explained Amex’s VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy, Hannah Bozian, in an interview with TechCrunch. She said the company wanted to ensure that agentic transactions are still “seamless, trusted, and secure, the way our card members expect them to be.”

This framework’s release follows the company’s April launch of Amex’s Agentic Commerce Experiences, or the ACE Developer Toolkit, which includes a handful of services that now include the intent framework.

Amex said it has not yet seen an increase in disputes because of agentic commerce, but it wanted to be proactive in building this technology as this type of commerce scales. In part, that’s because consumers have signaled they’re open to trying agentic commerce.

In a recent Amex Trendex report, 66% of surveyed U.S. consumers said they’re likely to use AI agents to research the best price for a product or service, and 61% said they’re likely to use it for a product or service recommendation over the next 12 months, the company told TechCrunch.

To start, Amex’s new intent framework begins with a Create Intent API, which will capture the customer’s purchase instructions along with other constraints they may have included in their request, like the merchant’s name, maximum budget, and other product preferences. How this intent is collected may vary depending on the AI model involved, but the plan is to make this framework flexible enough to support all agentic commerce models, Bozian said.

The customer then authenticates their identity and signs off on the intent captured by the agent.

Then an Intent ID, a unique identifier representing the intent, is created, along with a Proof of Intent Token, which includes the customer’s high-level constraints. This token is used to obtain a secure digital payment credential that the agent will use at checkout instead of the customer’s actual credit card number. In doing so, Amex says, the purchase will remain secure while being aligned with what the customer authorized the agent to do.

This Intent ID and token can also be used in different parts of the transaction process, helping companies to manage areas like fraud prevention and dispute resolution, Amex said.

“Our approach differs from the implementations of others in that it pulls intent earlier into the transaction flow. And this is important because it helps mitigate some risk before the risk occurs,” said Bozian. She offered the example of a customer asking an agent to buy white Nike sneakers in a size 9, but the agent submits a request to purchase shoes from Adidas. In such a case, Amex could prevent the transaction from going through because the agent made a mistake.

Bozian also notes that while many agents today ask for customer consent before making a purchase, Amex foresees a future where agents may act much more autonomously in some cases. For instance, a consumer might allow their agent to re-order household staples, like paper towels or toilet paper — categories in which the only real constraint is the price and size, not merchant or brand. In these scenarios, it makes sense to have technology in the loop performing that extra check, to ensure the transactions match the customer’s intent.

Having a log of what was authorized by which agent and when could also help address fraud on behalf of the agent, she noted.

Amex is already in discussions with partners across the payments ecosystem for implementing ACE, which includes the agentic tokens that contain Amex’s payment credentials, as well as other parts of the developer kit.

The company said it plans to actively develop ACE further as the agentic commerce ecosystem evolves.

On October 13 atTechCrunch Disrupt 2026‘s Industry Stage, Amex VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy at American Express, Hannah Bozian, will discuss the company’s new “Intent Intelligence Framework” in more detail, and what it means for the world of agentic commerce.

articles.title: Apple launches a new Apple TV 4K with Siri AI and remote-free voice commands
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.content:
Apple launched a new $299 Apple TV 4K streaming device today, with an upgraded chip, integration with the updated version of Siri AI for content discovery, and mics that allow users to issue voice commands directly without using the remote.

The refreshed Apple TV 4K comes with an upgraded A19 chip to enable various AI features. Hardware-wise, the new streaming box comes with three far-field microphones, letting users talk with Siri without a remote or a paired HomePod.

The company said that users can now have a four-speaker surround sound experience with Apple TV 4K  and HomePod mini 2 or HomePod 2 speakers.

The remote also gets a welcome update: It now includes a small speaker. This helps users find the remote easily when it gets lost in the nooks and corners of the couch or when they leave the remote in another room while doing a chore. (Apple added a way to find the remote withSiri and Find My in 2023, but it hinged on showing directions in the app rather than an audible sound.)

With Siri AI now rolling out to all Apple platforms, the big draw for Apple is to utilize it for better personalization and content recommendations. On the Apple TV, viewers can ask questions like “Which Apple TV shows won at the Emmy Awards this year?” to search for content, or ask for more information about shows with questions like “Where was ‘Pluribus’ filmed?”

RivalsGoogleandAmazonhave also added AI for content suggestions in the past few years.

The device is not updated as often as other Apple hardware, given thislong-pending upgrade comes four yearsafter the launch of Apple TV 4K in 2022.Bloombergreported that the company wanted to launch the new device in 2024, but delays in launching the AI-powered Siri forced Apple to push the launch of new home devices as well.

Consumers can preorder the new Apple TV 4K starting today, and the device will be available on November 13.

articles.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
articles.author: Russell Brandom
articles.content:
Meta’s Superintelligence Lab releaseda pair of new state-of-the-art modelson Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model.

Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

According to Meta’s testing (presented inthe model card), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

“Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads.

That scale is reflected in the pricing: Accessed through the Meta Model API, Wonder will cost $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, making it roughly equivalent in cost to GPT-6 Sol or Opus 5.5.

Notably, Wonder Full will only be available to Muse Code subscribers and will not be served through the API. Both models will also be used to power the Muse agent.

In keeping with Meta’s interest in developing personal assistants that can perform tasks over a long period, the company placed particular emphasis on the new models’ ability to retain and synthesize information given by the user, a property Meta calls “active memory.”

To achieve better recall, Meta highlightedthe MemoryBench benchmark, which challenges continual learning and memory construction frameworks. According to the company’s testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus, or Astra.

“We put a tremendous amount of effort into making sure your model can remember what’s important to you over days, weeks, months, and beyond,” said research scientist Kavya Kopparapu in a video accompanying the launch.

The new models are the first frontier model release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta’s AI effortsin August of last year. Since then, Meta has released its lightweight Muse Spark model andMuse agentbut has avoided the kind of state-of-the-art model releases OpenAI and Anthropic are known for.

According to the post, the models were trained at Meta’sPrometheus data center in central Ohio, which came online earlier this year.

articles.title: Affected by layoffs? Don’t miss this $75 deal for your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Expo+ Pass
articles.author: TechCrunch Events
articles.content:
If you’ve been laid off, you can get a TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Expo+ Pass for just $75. The offer is limited to the first 100 qualifying people, or until Disrupt doors open on October 13 at 8 a.m. PT. Once all 100 passes are claimed, the offer is no longer available.

Join 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leadersat San Francisco’s Moscone West on October 13-15, and put yourself back in the room where new opportunities are taking shape. Meet companies and people who could help open your next door, build your network, discover new career paths, and get a closer look at what’s happening across the startup and tech ecosystem.

Don’t let a layoff keep you on the sidelines.Come to Disrupt, meet new people, explore new opportunities, and take your next step.Grab your Layoff Expo+ Passbefore all 100 are claimed, or by the time Disrupt kicks off on October 13.

When you’re in between jobs, networking can be critical. Disrupt gives you three full days to make meaningful connections in one place.

At the center of Disrupt is the Expo Hall, where all 10,000+ attendees converge — founders, investors, tech leaders, innovators, and builders. Explore 300+ exhibiting startups, connect directly with founders and tech leaders, learn about new companies, andput yourself in the room for your next career opportunity.

You don’t have to wait until Disrupt to grow your network.Start networking as soon as you buy your ticketand download the TechCrunch Events app. Use the app’s AI-powered matchmaking to discover relevant people and make connections based on your interests and goals. Then take those connections offline through 1:1 meetings, conversations in the Expo Hall, and events throughout Disrupt.

Get practical insights through breakout sessionsand get your questions answered directly by the tech leaders shaping the startup and technology landscape. Take what you learn back to your job search, your next interview, or your next career move.

Disrupt isn’t just about finding an open role. It’s a chance to meet people you wouldn’t encounter through a job board, learn about companies before you apply, and put yourself in conversations that can lead somewhere unexpected.

YourExpo+ Passgives you access to:

Learn more and secure your pass before they’re all claimed.

The Expo+ Pass is designed to help you get into the heart of Disrupt, but it does not include access toindustry stages and roundtable sessions.

Want the full conference experience?Explore our other ticket optionsfor access to additional Disrupt programming and experiences.
